newsitem.title: INDIA: India flash floods kill 110, toll to rise.
newsitem.headline: India flash floods kill 110, toll to rise.

text.p: At least 110 people were killed in Tuesday's flash floods in a remote Himalayan region in northern India, and the toll could rise to 150, a senior police official said.
"I have a list of 110 persons who have been identified so far," a senior police official of Himachal Pradesh state told Reuters on Wednesday.
"I suspect the toll could be much higher. It could even be 150, when reports come from cut-off areas," he said.
Authorities had said on Tuesday that at least 135 people were missing, feared dead, after monsoon rains flooded the Chirgaon region, some 125 km (80 miles) east of the state capital of Shimla.
They said floods paralysed communications and swept away bridges, buildings and the whole shopping area in Chirgaon.
The police official said the floods had created a five square km (two square mile) lake on the river Sutlej at Wangtu, 200 km (125 miles) east of Shimla.

The official, who did not want to be identified, said the administration in the state had warned authorities managing the Bhakra Nangal Dam on the Sutlej river of possible flooding down stream in the state Punjab.
The official said 12 villages in the Shimla and Kinnaur districts of the state had been submerged.
He said the government has been moving people to safety in the higher regions. "Fortunately, the weather is favourable," he added.
The state has asked the army for help with rescue and relief operations.
